title: Rebuild current skill state after compaction and recovery
objective: Start a new context epoch after compact/recovery, rebuild the current full catalog snapshot, and retain only model-visible loaded-skill state.
context: Complete one low-conflict slice of the accepted live skill catalog and cache-preserving design.
The worktree is shared and dirty; only owned_files may be modified.

source_evidence.note: Developer-context initial catalog and progressive disclosure inspiration.
Live discovery, visibility overrides, and skill lifecycle inspiration.

include: Advance context_epoch whenever visible history is replaced.
Reinsert the current catalog snapshot instead of relying on a stale announced cursor.
Carry forward bounded latest invoked skill bodies/digests only when they are actually reattached.
Recover only exact full or superseding invocation envelopes that were model-visible before replacement; an already-loaded acknowledgement is not proof that a body survived.
Validate every candidate body against the current authoritative stable ID/content digest and omit disabled, revoked, shadowed, stale, malformed, or over-budget candidates.
Rebuild the loaded ledger only from exact invocation bodies that are present in the installed post-compact history.

Hold a Manager read transaction across authoritative snapshot, candidate sanitization, history installation, and cursor/ledger rebuild so refresh or visibility writes cannot invalidate the installed epoch midway.

Strip untrusted or stale skill-looking compact attachments and accept standalone restored bodies only through validated internal reattachment provenance; validate any ToolResult pairing selector against the envelope stable ID or unambiguous name.
Clear revoked/obsolete loaded digests and handle automatic, manual, reactive, and recovery compaction consistently.
Clear the OpenAI Responses previous_response_id chain on every history replacement while preserving the stable session PromptCacheKey.
exclude: Do not modify production files owned by another task.
Do not add dependencies or perform unrelated refactors.

implementation_steps: Wire epoch reset into all compact/recovery exits.
Extract the latest exact model-visible full/superseding envelope per stable ID, apply deterministic count/byte budgets, and attach only candidates still authorized by the current registry.
After installing the rebuilt history, reconstruct the loaded ledger from the exact retained or reattached bodies rather than the pre-compact in-memory ledger.
Add a read-only Manager snapshot transaction whose callback receives a defensive snapshot and cannot re-enter Manager; run the entire post-compact projection install inside it.
Use current registry inputs supplied by runtime hooks; do not invent a second registry.
Add automatic, manual, recovery, revoked-body, missing-history, untrusted-attachment, selector-pairing, and snapshot-to-install writer-race tests.
acceptance_criteria: Post-compact model always receives a current full snapshot.
A prior loaded digest cannot suppress body injection after its message left visible history.
Already-loaded acknowledgement messages are never promoted into body evidence after replacement.
A concurrent refresh, disable, or content update cannot interleave between the snapshot used to authorize restored bodies and installation of the new visible epoch.
Compactor-provided or malformed skill-looking attachments cannot bypass authoritative reattachment validation.
Catalog/body budgets remain bounded and selection is deterministic.
Every compact/recovery replacement clears previous_response_id chaining without changing PromptCacheKey.
risks: Compaction is a deliberate cache break; optimize correctness and bounded rebuild rather than pretending the old prefix survives.
dispatch_prompt: Implement context-epoch-aware post-compaction/recovery skill catalog and body restoration across only the owned compact/loop lifecycle files.
notes_for_assignee: If verification exposes a defect in another owner's production file, report the exact failing test and owner task; do not patch across ownership boundaries.
